product: a Christian video-streaming and discipleship app for iPhone and Android phones

namespaces.Common: Shared controls that many screens of the mobile app use, such as the back button in the top bar.
namespaces.VideoLabel: A short label that names the kind of video (for example a feature film or an episode). It shows on Home cards, and in capital letters above the title on the watch page.
namespaces.DownloadQuality: The video quality choices in the download sheet, where the viewer picks how large an offline copy or a saved file is.
namespaces.Subtitles: The subtitle control on the watch page and the subtitle choice in the download sheet.
namespaces.Profile: The Profile tab, which shows the viewer's account, the list of downloaded videos, and a link to the privacy policy. It also holds links to the organization's web pages.
namespaces.Auth: Sign-in and sign-out text in the Profile tab, and the small banner on the watch page that asks a signed-out viewer to sign in so the app keeps their place in a video.
namespaces.DeleteAccount: The account deletion steps in the Profile tab: the confirmation, the request to sign in again, and the result messages. The deletion is permanent, so the text must be exact.
namespaces.BibleReader: The Bible reader screen, which shows one verse at a time. It has a top bar (back, the passage, the translation, download, settings), a footer with the chapter and a verse counter, swipe hints, a verse selection bar with Copy and Share, and error messages. Book names and Bible text come from each translation, not from these strings.
namespaces.BiblePassagePicker: A sheet over the Bible reader where the viewer chooses a book, then a chapter, then a verse.
namespaces.BibleTranslationPicker: A sheet over the Bible reader where the viewer chooses a Bible translation. Each row shows which books the translation has and whether it is on the device.
namespaces.BibleReaderSettings: The Bible reader's settings sheet: color mode, text size, typeface, line spacing, verse numbers, and arrow buttons.
namespaces.BibleDownload: A system alert that downloads a Bible translation to the device, shows the progress, removes it, or explains why a download stopped.
namespaces.LapseReminder: A phone notification that the app sends one day or seven days after the viewer last used it, to invite them back to the last video they watched.
namespaces.Explore: The Explore tab: a full-screen vertical feed of short video clips. The viewer swipes up for the next clip. White text and round buttons sit over the playing video.
namespaces.Series: The series page: a trailer or a poster, the series title, buttons for language, subtitles, download, and share, and a grid of episode cards. It also holds the menus and alerts that manage the downloads of a series, and the language and subtitle sheets.
namespaces.SeriesDownload: A sheet that downloads every episode of a series at once, or saves all of them as files in a folder on the device. It shows the quality and subtitle choices, the progress of the check, and a summary of the result.
namespaces.DownloadSheet: The download sheet of one video, and the parts that the series download sheet also uses: the choice between an offline copy in the app and a file saved on the device, the quality and subtitle lists, the terms-of-use checkbox, and the terms window. The terms themselves stay in English.
namespaces.DownloadButton: The spoken label of the round download button on a video page and on a series page. It names the state of the download and what a tap does. Only a screen reader reads it.
namespaces.Library: The list of downloaded videos in the Profile tab. Each row shows the size and the state of one download. The viewer can select videos and delete them.
namespaces.ExportReport: A small card at the bottom of the screen that reports the result after the app saves a video file, or every episode of a series, in a folder on the device.

Subtitles.off.composition: Shows in the subtitle control when no subtitle track plays. Keep it as short as the language allows.

Subtitles.noSubtitles.composition: Shows in place of the subtitle choice when the video has no subtitle track.

Auth.signInComingSoonAriaLabel.composition: The screen reader reads the button name, the state, and the reason as one label.

BibleReader.chapterOpenedAriaAnnouncemen.composition: {chapter} is a book name and a chapter number, for example John 4.

BibleReader.choosePassageAriaLabel.composition: {passage} is a Bible reference, for example John 3:16. The screen reader reads the reference, then what the button does.

BibleReader.verseAriaValue.composition: {chapter} is a book name and a chapter number, for example John 3.

BibleReader.versesAriaValue.composition: One stop covers a range of verses. {chapter} is a book name and a chapter number.

BibleReader.verseAriaLabel.composition: {text} is the Bible text of the verse.

BibleReader.versesAriaLabel.composition: One stop covers a range of verses. {text} is their Bible text.

BiblePassagePicker.bookWithNoteAriaLabel.composition: {name} is a book name and {note} is a short note about it. Keep only the separator that the language uses between two phrases.

BibleTranslationPicker.twoNames.composition: Joins two Bible book names, for example Ruth and Luke.

BibleTranslationPicker.threeNames.composition: Joins three Bible book names, for example Ruth, Luke, and John.

BibleReaderSettings.textSizeAriaUnit.composition: The screen reader says a number, then this unit, for example 30 points. A point is a unit of text size.

BibleReaderSettings.lineSpacingAriaUnit.composition: The screen reader says a number, then this unit, for example 140 percent.

BibleReaderSettings.typefaceSerif.composition: A typeface with serifs. The option shows in that typeface.

BibleReaderSettings.typefaceSans.composition: A sans-serif typeface. The option shows in that typeface. Keep it short.

BibleReaderSettings.modeTrueDark.composition: A dark mode with a pure black background, darker than the Dark mode.

LapseReminder.channelName.composition: Shows in the phone's notification settings for this app. Keep it short.

Auth.signInPromptMessage.composition: Promise only that the app keeps the viewer's place from now on. Never say that it keeps the place in the video they just watched: that place is not saved.

DeleteAccount.failedMessage.composition: The deletion stops at the first failed step, so nothing was changed. {email} is a support email address.

DeleteAccount.reauthFailedMessage.composition: The deletion did not start. Keep it clearly different from the message for a failed deletion.

DeleteAccount.wrongAccountMessage.composition: A different account signed in, so the app deleted nothing. The original account still exists.

DeleteAccount.unconfirmedMessage.composition: The app cannot tell whether the server finished the deletion. Do not say that it did or that it did not.

Explore.mute.composition: A caption under a round sound button. The button turns the clip's sound off. At most two short lines.

Explore.unmute.composition: A caption under a round sound button. The button turns the clip's sound back on. At most two short lines.

Explore.share.composition: A caption under a round share button. At most two short lines.

Explore.nextClipAriaLabel.composition: The screen reader offers it on the clip. It moves to the next clip, like a swipe up.

Explore.previousClipAriaLabel.composition: The screen reader offers it on the clip. It moves back to the previous clip, like a swipe down.

Explore.descriptionMore.composition: Shows after the one visible line of a cut clip description, and opens the full description. Lower case in English. Keep it one short word.

Explore.descriptionLess.composition: Shows under an open clip description, and closes it to one line. Lower case in English. Keep it one short word.

Explore.progressAriaValue.composition: The screen reader reads it as the value of the clip progress bar. {elapsed} and {length} are whole seconds, for example 6 of 27 seconds.

Explore.emptyTitle.composition: {languageName} is the name of the viewer's feed language, for example Swahili. It can arrive in English, so never inflect it.

Series.thisSeries.composition: Takes the place of the series title in removeDownloadsMessage and as a menu title when the series has no title. Lower case in English.

Series.savedOfflineAriaLabel.role: episode state for a screen reader
Series.savedOfflineAriaLabel.composition: Follows the episode title after a comma, so it starts in lower case in English.

SeriesDownload.episodesInLanguage.composition: {language} is the name of a language, for example Swahili. It can arrive in English, so never inflect it.

SeriesDownload.startedCount.composition: One part of a summary line. The app joins the parts with a middle dot, for example: 12 started · 1 switched · 3 already downloaded.

DownloadSheet.agreeToTerms.composition: {terms} is a link with the text of termsLink (Terms of Use). Put {terms} where the link belongs in the sentence.

DownloadSheet.optionsAriaLabel.composition: {section} is a list heading, for example Quality.

DownloadSheet.saveToFiles.composition: Files is the name of Apple's Files app.

DownloadSheet.unknownSize.composition: Shows in place of a file size, such as 1.5 GB, when the size is not known.

DownloadButton.downloadingAtAriaLabel.composition: {percent} is a whole number from 1 to 100.

Library.downloadedStatus.composition: {size} is a file size, for example 74 MB.

Library.failedCount.composition: Follows the size of a series in a gray line, for example: 3 videos · 1.5 GB · 2 failed. Keep the middle dot at the start.

ExportReport.savedToFolder.composition: {folder} is the name of the folder that the viewer picked, for example Downloads.
